options.text: A newly created notebook based on a labeled lakehouse can inherit the label upon creation in supported flows.
options.why: Documented non-Power BI creation scenario.

options.text: Adding a new connection to an existing Fabric item can cause its sensitivity label to be re-evaluated.
options.why: The current information-protection design supports update/relationship reevaluation with limitations.

options.text: Every label always follows any external CSV exported by a notebook.
options.why: Native Fabric exports do not uniformly carry labels.

options.text: A downstream Power BI report can inherit from a labeled Fabric source through a supported relationship, subject to limitations.
options.why: Fabric→Power BI propagation is supported.

explanation: Creation, existing-item changes, and export are different label-lifecycle mechanisms. Avoid blanket guarantees across all item/export paths.

title: Workspace lineage boundary
prompt: A warehouse in Workspace A supports a report in Workspace B. A developer opens the workspace lineage diagram in A but does not see the downstream report. What should they do?

options.text: Assume the report is disconnected because workspace lineage is exhaustive for every workspace.
options.why: Workspace lineage does not show downstream items in other workspaces.

options.text: Use impact analysis on the warehouse to investigate downstream dependencies across workspaces.
options.why: Impact analysis supports the broader blast-radius view.

options.text: Turn on a sensitivity label to force the external report into the same workspace graph.
options.why: A label is not a lineage-visibility workaround.

options.text: Add a tag named B to the warehouse so remote dependencies materialize.
options.why: Tags do not create graph relationships.

explanation: Workspace lineage is primarily workspace scoped, with external connections only one level upstream. Impact analysis is the appropriate way to assess cross-workspace downstream dependencies.

title: Go-live risk triage
prompt: A finance team wants to certify a new semantic model and make it visible tenant-wide before quarter close. There is no evidence of an approved metric definition; the semantic model is also marked Confidential. What is the safest governance plan?

options.text: Validate the metrics and owner/steward approval; obtain certification from an authorized reviewer; configure discoverability separately; retain appropriate access and information-protection controls.
options.why: This separates trust review, discovery and information security.

options.text: Let any Contributor self-certify, then grant everyone Build to simplify discovery.
options.why: Reviewer authorization and least privilege are bypassed.

options.text: Apply a Certified text tag, which is equivalent to a Certified endorsement and automatically opens access.
options.why: Tags are not endorsements or access grants.

options.text: Remove the Confidential label before certification because the two states cannot coexist.
options.why: Sensitivity label and endorsement are independent dimensions.

explanation: A high-assurance rollout needs evidence of metric quality, authorized endorsement, deliberate discoverability, and independently enforced access/protection.
